turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The dominant signal is the processing route, not the composition.**
Sorting by `target`, the data splits into three clear regimes:

| Regime | Signature | target range |
|---|---|---|
| As-normalized / no heat treat | THT=30, CT=30, DT=30, TT=30 | 225–275 |
| Through-hardened + high temper | THT≈825–865, TT=550–680, Tt=60, TCr=24 | 325–650 |
| Low-temper / spring-steel type | THT=845, TT=420–500 | 688–874 |
| **Carburized + quenched + low-temp temper** | NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, **CT=930, Ct>0, DT≈850–896, Dt>0, QmT=60–140, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5** | **838–1190** |

Every one of the top ~25 samples is the carburizing route. So the recipe must sit in that branch: NT=930, THT=30/THt=0/THQCr=0, CT=930 (max), long carburizing time Ct, diffusion DT≈896, Dt=70.2, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5.

**2. Within the carburized group**, the trends are:
- `TT`: 160 ≥ 200 (lower temper temp slightly better); keep TT=160, Tt=120.
- `Ct` large (450–540) and `Dt` large (70.2) → the highest values (1120, 1144, 1190 all have Ct ≥ 340 with either Dt=70.2 or DT=850/Dt=15). Long carburize + long diffusion is favourable.
- `QmT`: 140 appears in 1190, 1054, 1068, 1080; ~neutral-to-positive → take 140.
- Alloying: the two best families are **high Ni (1.62–1.69) + Cr≈0.5–0.6 + Mo≈0.17–0.21** (1034, 1054, 1056, 1082, 1124, **1190**) and **low Ni + Cr≈1.14–1.17 + Mo≈0.17** (1068, 1080, 1104, **1144**). Both hardenability boosters; I combine them at a moderately aggressive but not fully extrapolated level (Ni≈1.65, Cr≈0.95, Mo≈0.20).
- Base C stays **low (0.17–0.23)** — the surface is carburized, so a low-carbon core is what the best samples use. Si/Mn/Cu near the group means; P and S low (best rows have P≈0.002–0.015, S≈0.012–0.016).
- Inclusion ratings `dA, dB, dC` small is mildly better (cleanliness); RedRatio around 440–860 in the best rows → take ~690.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=520, DT=895.812, Dt=70.2, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.31, Mn=0.65, P=0.005, S=0.012, Ni=1.65, Cr=0.95, Cu=0.10, Mo=0.20, RedRatio=690, dA=0.02, dB=0.0, dC=0.0**
